2. STEP 1 — INDEPENDENT DESIGN CLASSIFICATION & TOOL SELECTION (`RISK_OF_BIAS.md` §1):
   Classify the study's actual design from its Methods section, then select the matching appraisal tool:
   - `"RoB 2 (parallel-trial variant)"`: Individually randomized controlled trial. Rate all 5 domains (`D1` Randomization process; `D2` Deviations from intended interventions; `D3` Missing outcome data; `D4` Measurement of the outcome; `D5` Selection of the reported result) as `"Low"`, `"Some concerns"`, or `"High"`, and overall rating as `"Low"`, `"Some concerns"`, or `"High"`.
   - `"RoB 2 (cluster-randomized trials variant)"`: Cluster-randomized trial (villages, compounds, neighbourhoods, schools, utilities randomized as clusters). Rate all 6 domains (`D1a` Randomization process; `D1b` Timing of identification or recruitment of participants within clusters; `D2` Deviations from intended interventions; `D3` Missing outcome data; `D4` Measurement of the outcome; `D5` Selection of the reported result) as `"Low"`, `"Some concerns"`, or `"High"`, and overall rating as `"Low"`, `"Some concerns"`, or `"High"`.
   - `"ROBINS-I"`: Non-randomized study of an intervention / policy with a genuine comparator (DiD, IV, RDD, PSM, ITS, controlled before-after, comparative longitudinal/panel evaluation). Rate all 7 domains (`D1` Bias due to confounding; `D2` Bias in selection of participants into the study; `D3` Bias in classification of interventions; `D4` Bias due to deviations from intended interventions; `D5` Bias due to missing data; `D6` Bias in measurement of outcomes; `D7` Bias in selection of the reported result — note `No information` honestly if no pre-analysis plan/protocol exists) as `"Low"`, `"Moderate"`, `"Serious"`, `"Critical"`, or `"No information"`, and overall rating in the same vocabulary. Do NOT assign single-case histories with no comparator arm to ROBINS-I!
   - `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross Sectional Studies"`: Quantitative cross-sectional survey / observational regression without a quasi-experimental intervention structure. Rate all 8 items (`Q1` Inclusion criteria in sample clearly defined; `Q2` Study subjects and setting described in detail; `Q3` Exposure measured validly and reliably; `Q4` Objective, standard criteria used for measurement of condition; `Q5` Confounding factors identified; `Q6` Strategies to deal with confounding factors stated; `Q7` Outcomes measured validly and reliably; `Q8` Appropriate statistical analysis used) as `"Yes"`, `"No"`, `"Unclear"`, or `"Not applicable"`. Provide overall narrative judgment (`"Low concern"`, `"Some concern"`, or `"High concern"` — no numeric score).
   - `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Cohort Studies"`: Observational comparative cohort design (not framed as a ROBINS-I intervention). Rate all 11 items (`Q1` Similar groups from same population; `Q2` Exposures measured similarly; `Q3` Exposure measured validly/reliably; `Q4` Confounding factors identified; `Q5` Strategies to deal with confounding stated; `Q6` Participants free of outcome at start; `Q7` Outcomes measured validly/reliably; `Q8` Follow-up time reported and sufficient; `Q9` Follow-up complete or loss explored; `Q10` Strategies to address incomplete follow-up utilized; `Q11` Appropriate statistical analysis used) as `"Yes"`, `"No"`, `"Unclear"`, or `"Not applicable"`, plus narrative overall judgment (`"Low concern"`, `"Some concern"`, `"High concern"`).
   - `"CASP Qualitative Checklist"`: Primary qualitative study (interviews, ethnography, focus groups, qualitative documentary/field case study). Rate all 10 items (`Q1` Clear statement of aims; `Q2` Qualitative methodology appropriate; `Q3` Research design appropriate to address aims; `Q4` Recruitment strategy appropriate to aims; `Q5` Data collected in a way that addressed research issue; `Q6` Relationship between researcher and participants adequately considered [reflexivity]; `Q7` Ethical issues considered; `Q8` Data analysis sufficiently rigorous; `Q9` Clear statement of findings; `Q10` How valuable is the research [narrative assessment]). Rate Q1-Q9 `"Yes"`, `"No"`, or `"Can't tell"`, and Q10 narratively; give narrative `overall_rating` (e.g. `"Low methodological concern"`, `"Moderate concern (X Can't tell / No items)"`, `"High methodological concern"` — no numeric score).
   - `"MMAT (Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool)"`: Genuine mixed-methods primary study combining qualitative AND quantitative empirical components (do NOT assign purely quantitative or purely qualitative studies to MMAT). Rate Screening `S1`-`S2`, Qualitative `1.1`-`1.5`, the matching Quantitative 5-item block (`2.1`-`2.5` randomized, `3.1`-`3.5` non-randomized, or `4.1`-`4.5` descriptive), AND Mixed-Methods integration `5.1`-`5.5` (`5.1` adequate rationale for mixed methods; `5.2` components effectively integrated; `5.3` outputs of integration adequately interpreted; `5.4` divergences/inconsistencies adequately addressed; `5.5` components adhere to quality criteria of each tradition) as `"Yes"`, `"No"`, or `"Can't tell"`. Per MMAT 2018 rules, NEVER compute a numeric score; provide a concise criterion-grounded narrative `overall_rating` noting that overall quality cannot exceed the weakest component.
   - `"AMSTAR 2"`: Secondary systematic review, meta-analysis, or scoping review with an explicit systematic search/screening method (NEVER apply AMSTAR 2 to non-systematic narrative literature reviews!). Rate all 16 items `Q1`-`Q16` (explicitly marking critical domains `Q2`, `Q4`, `Q7`, `Q9`, `Q11`, `Q13`, `Q15`) as `"Yes"`, `"Partial Yes"` (where applicable), `"No"`, or `"Not applicable (no meta-analysis)"`, and apply AMSTAR 2 overall confidence (`"High"`, `"Moderate"`, `"Low"`, `"Critically Low"`).
   - `"Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework"`: Doctrinal-empirical hybrid, jurimetric analysis, or institutional/legal-historical case study that fits NONE of the six conventional designs above. Explicitly frame `overall_rating` as a structured non-validated judgment (NEVER a numeric composite score!).
   - `"NONE"`: Use when the study fits NONE of the listed instruments (e.g., pure mathematical/simulation optimization model with no empirical sample, or non-systematic narrative essay/review with no primary empirical method and no systematic search). cross_tool_domains.attrition: Serious concern: Although the target population comprises all 53 municipalities in Caldas, Quindio, and Risaralda, missing administrative records and database start-date truncations reduce the analyzed sample to 33 of 53 municipalities (62.3%) for aqueduct and sewerage subscribers and coverage (with several included series further shortened from 5 to 4 annual observations), 42 of 53 municipalities (79.2%) for IRCA water quality risk, and 52 of 53 for SGP transfers, using complete-case exclusion with no sensitivity analysis.
cross_tool_domains.confounding: Critical concern: Each municipality is evaluated via an isolated univariate robust paired-samples t-test (df = 2 or 3) comparing 5 annual observations up to the cadastral update year against 5 annual observations after the update year, with no unexposed control group, no adjustment for secular time trends or inflation in fiscal series, and no control for concurrent municipal tax statute reforms, arrears recovery campaigns, early-payment incentives, SGP indigenous-reserve/poverty formulas, or urban population growth.
cross_tool_domains.legal_measurement_quality: Moderate quality: Cadastral updating dates are drawn from official IGAC (2020) administrative records and contextualized within Colombian statutory mandates (Ley 1450 de 2011 art. 24 five-year updating rule, Ley 1176 de 2007 SGP water/sanitation allocation criteria, Decreto 416 de 2007, and Ley 1430 de 2010, alongside a minor typo citing Ley 715 as 2011 on PDF p. 6). However, the exposure is operationalized coarsely by placing the update year inside pre-update Period 1 without verifying fiscal implementation dates and by pooling 6 municipalities with asynchronous urban-only or rural-only updates against municipality-wide outcomes.
cross_tool_domains.measurement_bias: Serious concern: Administrative SUI subscriber data exhibit acknowledged inconsistencies and extreme outliers in 20 of the 33 analyzed municipalities (PDF p. 17, fn. 3) and yield degenerate test statistics (t = -Inf, Cohen's d = NaN) in Table 6; aqueduct and sewerage coverage relies on an unvalidated author-constructed proxy dividing subscribers by cadastral parcels (mechanically linking exposure and denominator, with Formula 1 blank/omitted on PDF p. 7); urban and rural subscribers cannot be disaggregated; and IRCA water quality changes are confounded by varying annual health-authority sampling intensity.
cross_tool_domains.outcome_measurement_quality: Weak / Serious concern: Water and sanitation outcomes rely on national administrative registries (SSPD-SUI for aqueduct/sewerage subscribers and INS-SIVICAP for IRCA), but suffer from severe SUI reporting outliers in 20/33 municipalities, an unrendered proxy coverage formula combining SUI subscribers with cadastral parcel counts, inability to separate urban from rural utility access, and fluctuating annual water-quality test counts across years.
cross_tool_domains.reporting_bias: Moderate concern: No pre-analysis plan or protocol is reported, ~300 separate municipality-level paired t-tests are conducted at unadjusted alpha = 0.05 without multiplicity correction, Formula 1 is missing from the published layout on PDF p. 7, IRCA sample window descriptions conflict across PDF pp. 7, 16, and 17, and Tables 2, 3, 4, and 7 truncate rows at 41-42 municipalities while narrative text reports totals out of 52-53 municipalities; however, null findings on property tax, aqueduct coverage, and IRCA are candidly reported and highlighted in the abstract and conclusions.
cross_tool_domains.selection_bias: Moderate concern: Selecting the complete census of all 53 municipalities in three Colombian departments (Caldas, Quindio, and Risaralda) prevents arbitrary cherry-picking at the study frame level, but conditioning inclusion in the SUI aqueduct/sewerage (33/53) and IRCA water quality (42/53) analyses on database availability from 2005/2007 onward systematically restricts WASH analyses to municipalities that updated their cadastres in later years.

domain_ratings.justification: The study uses isolated univariate robust paired-samples t-tests (df = 2.00 or 3.00) comparing one 5-year pre-update window against one 5-year post-update window within each municipality, with zero control group, zero detrending or inflation adjustment for fiscal revenues/transfers, and zero statistical control for secular urbanization dynamics, SGP statutory formula drivers (such as indigenous reserve allocations and NBI poverty), or concurrent municipal fiscal reforms (tax code updates under Ley 1450 de 2011, arrears collection drives, and early-payment discounts explicitly acknowledged by the author). Secular time trends are completely conflated with the intervention.

domain_ratings.domain_name: Bias in selection of participants into the study
domain_ratings.justification: The overall sampling frame covers all 53 municipalities in the departments of Caldas, Quindío, and Risaralda, avoiding discretionary selection into the primary frame. However, because SUI utility data begin in 2005 and INS IRCA data begin later, eligibility for the water and sanitation sub-analyses depends on the calendar year of cadastral updating (restricting eligible municipalities to later updaters: 38 eligible and 33 analyzed for aqueduct/sewerage; 42 analyzed for IRCA).

Cadastral update years are taken from official IGAC (2020) records, which is objective. However, the cadastral update year itself is grouped into pre-intervention Period 1 (Table 1) without verifying exact fiscal or administrative effective dates, and in 6 municipalities urban and rural cadastral updates were asynchronous (or urban-only/rural-only in Table 1) while all fiscal and utility outcomes are measured at the aggregate municipal level.

domain_ratings.domain_name: Bias due to deviations from intended interventions
domain_ratings.justification: In this observational evaluation of routine cadastral updating, the author notes that post-update fiscal and service changes co-occurred unevenly with municipal revenue statute reforms, delinquent-tax collection campaigns, taxpayer discounts, and national SGP transfers, none of which were measured or balanced across pre- and post-update periods.

Missing administrative data caused substantial exclusions: 20 of 53 municipalities (37.7%) were excluded from aqueduct and sewerage subscriber/coverage analyses (15 due to pre-2008 updates lacking SUI pre-period data and 5 more—Marmato, Norcasia, Pensilvania, Pueblo Rico, and Córdoba—explicitly dropped for missing data, plus several included municipalities reduced from 5 to 4 years), and 11 of 53 municipalities (20.8%) were excluded from IRCA water quality analyses, with no imputation or sensitivity checks.

domain_ratings.justification: Although data come from official national platforms (DNP, SSPD-SUI, INS-SIVICAP), three major measurement flaws exist: (1) SUI subscriber reports contain acknowledged inconsistencies and outliers in 20 of 33 analyzed municipalities (producing t = -Inf and Cohen's d = NaN in Table 6); (2) aqueduct and sewerage coverage is an author-constructed proxy based on subscribers and cadastral parcels reported in the cadastral update (mechanically coupling exposure and outcome denominator, with Formula 1 blank in the published PDF); and (3) IRCA risk scores are affected by varying annual sanitary-authority sampling counts and urban/rural outcomes cannot be disaggregated.

domain_ratings.domain_name: Bias in selection of the reported result
domain_ratings.justification: No pre-analysis plan exists, and roughly 300 separate municipal paired t-tests are evaluated at unadjusted p < 0.05. In addition, Tables 2, 3, 4, and 7 omit the final 10-11 municipalities in print while the text reports summary counts across 52-53 municipalities, Formula 1 is omitted on p. 7, and IRCA period descriptions vary across pp. 7, 16, and 17. Risk is rated Moderate rather than Serious because all six research questions are reported and the author prominently reports null effects for property tax (~49% null), aqueduct coverage (85% null), and IRCA.

raw_response.overall_narrative_summary: Pulgarín-Franco (2024) conducts a non-randomized longitudinal pre-post (uncontrolled before-after) administrative evaluation across the 53 municipalities of Caldas, Quindío, and Risaralda (Colombia), testing whether municipal cadastral updating changes property tax collection, national water/sanitation intergovernmental transfers (SGP), aqueduct and sewerage subscribers and coverage, and drinking-water quality risk (IRCA) across 5-year pre-update versus 5-year post-update windows. Appraised with ROBINS-I, the study is at Critical overall risk of bias. First, confounding bias (D1) is Critical: each municipality is analyzed separately with a univariate robust paired-samples t-test (df = 2 or 3) over a 10-year span without an unexposed comparator group, detrending, inflation adjustment, or control for urbanization, SGP statutory allocation formulas, municipal revenue code reforms, or tax-arrears recovery campaigns. Second, bias due to missing data (D5) and outcome measurement (D6) are both Serious: missing SUI and IRCA records exclude 37.7% of municipalities (20/53) from aqueduct/sewerage analyses and 20.8% (11/53) from water quality analyses; SUI subscriber series exhibit acknowledged outliers in 20 of 33 analyzed municipalities (yielding t = -Inf and NaN effect sizes in Table 6); utility coverage relies on a custom proxy combining SUI subscribers with cadastral parcel counts (whose Formula 1 is missing from the published page on PDF p. 7); urban and rural subscribers cannot be separated even where cadastral updates were urban-only or rural-only; and IRCA scores reflect changing health-authority water-sampling intensity. Selection of municipalities into sub-analyses (D2), intervention classification (D3), co-interventions (D4), and incomplete/truncated results tables without multiplicity adjustment (D7) pose Moderate concerns, though the author candidly reports predominantly null findings on aqueduct coverage and water quality.
raw_response.study_design_identified: Non-randomized longitudinal pre-post (uncontrolled before-after) administrative panel evaluation across 53 Colombian municipalities comparing 5-year pre-update and 5-year post-update periods using robust paired-samples t-tests
raw_response.where_found_summary: Study design, data sources (IGAC, DNP OEC/TerriData/SICODIS, SSPD-SUI, INS-SIVICAP), proxy coverage description, and statistical test (JAMOVI Walrus Robust Paired Samples T-Test) are in Metodología y Datos ([PDF Pages 6-7]). Municipality update cohorts and pre/post windows are in Tabla 1 ([PDF Page 8]), municipality-level t-test outputs and subgroup sample exclusions are in Resultados and Tablas 2-7 ([PDF Pages 8-16]), and data inconsistencies, SUI outliers (Footnote 3), proxy coverage rationale, urban/rural aggregation limits, and IRCA sampling gaps are in Conclusiones ([PDF Pages 16-17]).
raw_response.why_tool_chosen: The study empirically evaluates the effect of a specific legal/administrative intervention—municipal cadastral updating under Colombia's five-year statutory mandate (Ley 1450 de 2011, art. 24)—on municipal fiscal extraction and water/sewerage utility outcomes across 53 municipalities by comparing 5-year pre-update (Periodo 1) vs. 5-year post-update (Periodo 2) longitudinal observations. Because it is a quantitative non-randomized comparative pre-post evaluation of a policy intervention across multiple jurisdictions rather than a cross-sectional survey, qualitative study, or pure doctrinal essay, ROBINS-I is the exact matching appraisal tool.
